overview.text:
Chilika, a short drive from Puri, is Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon and was India's first Ramsar wetland, cut off from the Bay of Bengal by a 60-km strip of marshy islands and sand flats. Placed on the Montreux Record of threatened wetlands in 1993, it recovered and came off the list in 2002. Its sanctuary covers about 1,100 sq km, and in winter more than a million migratory birds — flamingos, pelicans, herons and storks — arrive; the lake is also home to the endangered Irrawaddy dolphin.

The main bases are Satapada, 50 km from Puri, for dolphin trips, and Mangalajodi, 75 km from Bhubaneswar, a community-run wetland for birdwatching by boat. Boats also visit Kalijai island's temple and Honeymoon and Breakfast islands. The sanctuary is open 6 am to 7 pm; come November to February for the birds.
